questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have always wanted to stay in Paris for a longer period of time and experience the French culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were not many courses in English available, so it was difficult for me to find courses I could take. And when I went to the university some courses overlapped, so it was not possbile for me to come to every class. I therefore missed out on some of the classes, which was unfortunate.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fine.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had a very good coordinator, Silvine Souchet, who always were good at helping when I had questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very difficult to find a place to stay in Paris. If you don't have any contacts, I would recommend just looking at Airbnbs and be aware that it is very expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is expensive

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Just because I didn't want to live in Cergy and I wouldn't recommend it. The city is not very safe and you don't want to go out at night there. It is a lot more safe in Paris and you get to experience Paris a lot more.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was fine.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A lot of help from my coordinator Silvine. Don't be afraid to ask questions. I wrote with her a lot.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I couldn't get a lot of the courses approved, it was difficult for me to find some that I did not already have in Denmark.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you can choose between multiple, just try out different courses in the beginning - it is possible to switch.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some were high level, some were not. Some were a bit difficult to follow, because I could not attend every class. It was nice that there were midterms and assignments during the year, because it was easier for me to study throughout the semester and pass the exams in the end, because I would not be too stressed about the grade.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different that we had to do assignments throughout the year and that they counted in the last grade. So

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Macroeconomics 1: Growth
Intertemporal risk and uncertainty
Applications of econometrics
Markets and organizations
Choice and Decision theory

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Markets and Organizations and applications of econometrics. It depends on what your interests are, but these were very interesting if you like econometrics and labor economics.

questions.answer: a lot but didn't try

questions.answer: don't know

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Museums and good restaurants in paris

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just be open to getting to know other people's cultures.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That NO other were scandinavien. We all had very different cultures. But it was interesting to get to know others.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I don't know

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: I would say NOT to stay in Cergy. It is not a nice city. Maybe try to find housing with other people living in Paris on exchange. Maybe from other cultures also and not just in the Danish house.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no don't think so

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To get to experience the culture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language - not many people from Cergy/Paris knows English. So it was very difficult. But the university offers free French Courses, if you want to try it out. I heard from others that they learned a lot.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
